MILEAGE LOG · WORKS OFFLINE · DATA STAYS ON YOUR DEVICE

A mileage log that would hold up if you were asked for it.

Log trips by odometer, by typing miles, or with GPS while the page is open. Every trip is priced at the IRS standard mileage rate for its own date (the 2026 business rate changed on July 1), the year is split into business, commuting and other miles for Schedule C Part IV, and the log is checked for the gaps an examiner looks for. Export a CSV any time. No account, no subscription.

Trips are stored in this browser only and never sent anywhere. Download a backup now and then: clearing browser data clears the log.

1. Year and odometer

Rates (override if the IRS changes them)

Leave blank to use the IRS rate for each trip's date. Verify current rates at irs.gov/tax-professionals/standard-mileage-rates.

Employee? Claim reimbursement from your employer

Since 2018 employees cannot deduct unreimbursed mileage on a federal return, so the useful document is a claim to your employer. It lists your business trips for a date range at your employer's per-mile rate (leave blank for the IRS rate on each trip's date) and downloads as a printable HTML page.

Repeat a trip

Your most frequent deductible routes. One tap fills the form for today; add the odometer or confirm the miles, then save.

2. Add a trip

Business, medical and charity trips need a destination and a purpose. GPS tracking only works while this page is open and the screen is on; it fills in the miles when you stop.

Summary

By vehicle

The standard rate is claimed per vehicle. Enter each vehicle's January 1 and December 31 odometer to get its own business-use share.

3. Export, back up, restore

The model, and what it leaves out

  • Deduction is each trip's miles times the IRS standard rate for the trip's date and category. Business, medical and charity trips are deductible at their rate; commuting and personal trips are not. Tolls and parking on business trips are shown separately because they are deductible in addition to the standard rate.
  • Odometer readings take priority over typed miles when both are present and the end is higher than the start.
  • Audit-readiness checks look at the log itself: deductible trips missing a purpose or destination, odometer readings that contradict each other, possible duplicates, a log made mostly of round numbers, entries typed long after the trip, and business miles that exceed the year's total.
  • Not modelled: whether the standard rate is available for your vehicle, the actual-expense method (see the mileage method calculator), state rules, employee reimbursement plans, and whether a particular trip is deductible at all.

Common questions

What does the IRS expect a mileage log to show?

For each business trip: the date, the miles, where you went and the business purpose, plus the odometer readings at the start and end of the year to prove the total. The IRS calls this adequate records or sufficient evidence, and a log written at or near the time of the trip carries the most weight.

Which rate does it use?

The IRS standard mileage rate for the date of each trip: 70 cents for 2025 business miles, 72.5 cents for January to June 2026 and 76 cents from July 1, 2026. Medical and charity rates are included and every rate can be overridden in the settings. Check irs.gov before you file.

Does it track my location in the background?

No. GPS tracking works only while this page is open and the screen stays on, and it only starts when you press Start. Nothing is uploaded: positions are used to add up the distance in your browser and are not stored. For unattended tracking a native app is still better; this tool is for a log you control.

Where is my data kept, and can I lose it?

In your browser on this device. Clearing site data, or a browser that clears storage for sites you have not opened in a while, removes it. Use Download backup regularly; the file restores on any device.

Can I use it offline?

Yes. Once the page has loaded it works with no signal, and you can add it to your home screen.

Is this tax advice?

No. It applies published rates to the trips you enter and checks your log for gaps. It does not decide whether a trip is deductible, whether the standard rate is available for your vehicle, or how to file.

No warranty. This tool is provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied. It is not legal, tax, or financial advice, and it does not replace a qualified professional. Results are estimates that depend entirely on the trips you enter and on IRS rates that change; confirm rates and rules at irs.gov or with a tax professional before you file.

Best-effort hosting, no SLA. These tools are free, experimental, and may be slow, broken, moved, or taken offline without notice. We do not promise uptime, backups of anything you type, or that a URL will keep working. Do not use this as your only record: download a backup.

Everything runs in your browser. Your trips are never uploaded; there are no accounts, cookies, or analytics vendors. GPS positions are used only to add up distance while you track and are not stored. Anonymous feature events (trip_saved, csv_exported, example_loaded) are counted only in local storage on your device, never the trips. Turn it off below, or with Do Not Track / Global Privacy Control.

Choosing between the standard rate and actual expenses? Try the mileage deduction method calculator. Driving for a delivery or rideshare app? See the gig driver net pay calculator.

Free and open source. If this helped, the code is under an MIT licence — support is entirely optional and never changes what the tool does.

privacy.html.text:
Mileage Log privacy policy

Applies to the Mileage Log web page and the Mileage Log phone app. Both are free, open source (MIT) software.

What does Mileage Log collect?

Nothing. There is no account, no sign-in, no advertising, no analytics and no server that receives your data. The people who publish this software do not receive your trips, your locations or your device identifiers.

Does Mileage Log track my location?

The phone app asks for location access, including in the background, so it can notice a drive and add up its distance. Positions are processed on the phone to find where a drive started and ended, and only the trip records you keep (date, places, distance, category) are stored, on the phone. Places are not looked up with any outside service. The web page uses location only while it is open and you press Start, and does not store positions.

Where your log lives

On your device only (browser storage or phone app storage). Backups and reports are files you choose to save or share; where they go after that is your choice. Deleting a trip removes it; uninstalling the app or clearing site data removes everything.

Sharing

We share nothing because we hold nothing. If you share a report with a tax preparer, you are sending it yourself.

Children

Not directed to children under 13.

Changes and contact

Changes are made in the public source repository and dated in its history. Questions: open an issue in the repository. This policy is not legal or tax advice, and Mileage Log is not tax advice.

No warranty. This tool is provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied. It is not legal, tax, or financial advice, and it does not replace a qualified professional. Results are estimates that depend entirely on the trips you enter and on IRS rates that change; confirm rates and rules at irs.gov or with a tax professional before you file.
